items.text:
Meta is claiming a research tax credit on its AI data centers, and the sums are large.

The New York Times reported the story and The Decoder wrote it up on 30 September. Meta classifies the data centers as "pilot models" and the Nvidia chips inside them as experimental materials. On that basis it saved $3.9 billion in 2025. It saved $2 billion in 2024 and $700 million in 2023. The Times reports that makes Meta the biggest beneficiary of this credit among all publicly traded companies.

The label sits awkwardly next to what Meta tells investors. In January 2025 Zuckerberg said these data centers would "drive our core products and business." By July he was announcing hundreds of billions in compute spending. One cluster, Hyperion, is supposed to scale to 5 GW over several years. Meta defends the credit by pointing to $200 billion of R&D spending over the past five years.

Meta's own filings hedge. The Decoder says SEC filings warn the savings could be challenged. It says reserves for uncertain tax positions jumped 45 percent to $18.74 billion. The credit itself comes from a 1981 law. James Shannon, the congressman who introduced it, told the Times it was meant for "people power, knowledge, information." EY audits Meta and approved the strategy. The Times reports that EY helped build the scheme and is now pitching the same approach to other companies offsetting AI chip purchases.

My read: hold the savings against the reserve. Add the three years the report gives and you get $6.6 billion. Reserves for uncertain tax positions stand at $18.74 billion. That reserve covers every uncertain position Meta carries. And 6.6 is three years of this one credit. So 6.6 over 18.74 is a lower bound on its share. Even at the lower bound this credit accounts for about a third of the pile.

four new Mini Apps just landed on @StartaleApp. the icons look like one lineup, but the apps give you four quite different things to do

Superstakefun’s SuperEngine is the one i want to look at first. you can choose an existing game format, then make the name, artwork, tiles and theme your own. you are working with established game mechanics, but the result can feel like something your community made.

Kabu Getaway goes straight to the chase. pick a route, dodge the cops and try to escape with your multiplier intact. it sounds like the kind of game you open for a quick round and end up replaying because you took the wrong turn.

Farm Frens takes its time. plant crops, raise animals and check in on a farm your friends can keep busy while you are away. i like that the reason to come back is the farm itself, rather than another button asking for a daily click.

MoonRush is the unusual addition here. it brings trader activity and market data into a lineup mostly built around games, alongside AI checks for risky tokens. i would treat those checks as a useful signal, not a reason to skip my own research.

i am curious about SuperEngine in particular. seeing what people actually make with it will tell me more than the launch graphic can

SCHWAB $SCHW IS $2.61 UNDER SEPTEMBER 22. THE YIELD MOVED:

Charles Schwab SCHW at $97.74, -$1.36 / -1.37% on Wednesday, and $97.75 premarket (as of 7:40am ET), +$0.01 / +0.01% from Wednesday's close. The Westlake, Texas firm holds brokerage accounts, and the idle cash in them, for retail investors and independent advisors. The September 22 note caught the shares at $100.36 an hour after the open. That day's regular close was $100.35. Wednesday is -$2.61 / -2.60% from that close, and it is the lowest close since. The verdict: the yield that morning did not have has arrived, the shares did not come back with it, and the cash figure that can test that is still the October 15 report.

Every regular close since that note has finished under $100.35.

- September 22: $100.35
- September 23: $99.50
- September 24: $99.49
- September 25: $99.03
- September 28: $98.30
- September 29: $99.10
- September 30: $97.74

Tuesday was the only up close, +$0.80. Wednesday's -$1.36 took that back and finished $0.56 under Monday's $98.30. The premarket penny means the low close is still the price before the open.

The 10-year Treasury yield, what the US government pays to borrow for 10 years, closed Wednesday at 5.293%, +3.8 basis points / +0.72% from Tuesday's 5.255%. A basis point is 0.01 percentage point. That print is the CBOE 10-year yield index, a market quote. The same index closed September 22 at 4.968%. Wednesday is 32.5 basis points above that close.

The Federal Reserve's own daily figure was 4.96% on September 22 and 4.96% on September 21. That is the unchanged yield the morning was looking at. The latest Fed figure, for September 29, is 5.26%, up 30 basis points from September 22. Wednesday's Fed figure is not out. The release that carries it lands later today.

iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) at $77.78, -$0.45 / -0.58% on Wednesday. That fund rises when long-term rates fall and drops when they rise. September 22's regular close was $81.75. Wednesday is -$3.97 / -4.86% from that close. The bond moved. Schwab, measured from its own September 22 close, did not move the other way.

June quarter, in the company's 10-Q, reported July 21. Net revenue, the top line, was $7.072B, up 21% from $5.851B. Net interest revenue, interest earned minus interest paid, was $3.357B, about 47.5% of that top line. A higher 10-year reaches that line as loans and bonds are reinvested. It does not reset the whole line on the day the yield jumps. The shares made their low with the yield already up.

On September 30 Schwab announced Charley, an assistant that answers clients in conversation. Beginning in October it rolls out in phases to eligible U.S. retail clients on https://t.co/JK1IxbCg1Y and the mobile app. At launch it handles questions, quotes, balances, and a short list of chores: watchlists, dividend reinvestment, beneficiaries, contact details, and alerts. It can also hand the client to a person. Schwab says the capabilities will grow, and that Charley may be inaccurate or incomplete, so the client should check the result. The published launch list does not include a higher rate on idle cash. The announcement is dated the same day as the $97.74 close. Same day is not the same as a cause.

Schwab's own survey, more than 500 clients and prospects with at least $10,000, taken September 21 through September 25, found 65% saying AI can do routine tasks or take a larger role if a person is still involved. Those respondents preferred a person for more meaningful account actions.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD) at $112.50, -$3.72 / -3.20% on Wednesday was the comparison that morning, unchanged then at $123.36. Its September 22 regular close was $124.25. Wednesday is -$11.75 / -9.46% from that close. From Monday, September 21, Schwab is -$9.14 / -8.55% and Robinhood is -$10.80 / -8.76%. The hour sorted the two. The closes since then did not. Robinhood fits none of the six Len5es. The Momentum Len5 hunts a stock climbing on real news, and a close $11.75 under September 22 is not that climb.

Schwab is a pick on none of the six either. The nearest is Quality-Value, which hunts a hard-to-copy business bought for less than it is worth. The hard-to-copy half is the account base. The September 17 release still had client assets at $13.41T as of August 31, and 40.1 million active brokerage accounts. No September asset count has replaced that. The price half fails. Stockholders' equity, the owners' stake, was $50.147B at June 30. Preferred stock, paid ahead of common holders, was $6.213B. Common equity was $43.934B. Divided by the 1,728 million shares outstanding at June 30, that is $25.42 a share. Wednesday's $97.74 is about 3.85 times that, a premium to the common stake, not a discount to it. The quarter's return on average common equity, profit on that stake, annualized, was 25%, on average common equity of $43.203B. What would put Schwab on the Quality-Value Len5: that 25% return holding for several quarters, October 15 included, with the shares no higher than $97.74.

The Quality Len5 is a profitable, stable business, and a low price is not required. It needs a stated gross profit, a profit on the owners' stake, and debt that does not exceed that stake. The 25% return is the profit on the stake. Long-term debt was $22.669B, other short-term borrowings $13.945B, and Federal Home Loan Bank borrowings $0.500B. Together that is $37.114B, under the $43.934B common stake. The June report does not state a gross profit, so the Quality Len5 is not met. What would put Schwab on the Quality Len5: a stated gross profit, with those borrowings still under $43.934B.

The Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5 hunts a price under a cautious reading of worth, or an event that changes the math. About 3.85 times the June common book is not under the stake. Charley is a product launch, not a price under $25.42. What would put Schwab on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5: a price near that $25.42 book with the account base still intact.

The Growth Len5 hunts rising profit the price has not already paid for. June diluted profit was $1.54 a share, against $1.08 a year earlier, the company's 43% gain. The shares are still about 3.85 times the June book, so the rise is not unpaid for. What would put Schwab on the Growth Len5: October 15 diluted profit above $1.54 with the shares still near $97.74.

The Hypergrowth Len5 hunts very fast sales growth at a size that is already real. Net revenue of $7.072B is that size. A 21% gain is not that speed. What would put Schwab on the Hypergrowth Len5: net revenue growing at a much faster pace from that $7.072B.

The Momentum Len5 hunts a stock climbing on real news. The closes run from $100.35 to $97.74, with one up day in between. What would put Schwab on the Momentum Len5: a close back above September 21's $106.88 after the October 15 report.

The Income Len5 hunts cash handed to owners that the business can keep paying. On July 23 the board declared $0.32 a share, paid August 28. Four checks at that rate are $1.28, about 1.31% of $97.74, against a 10-year at 5.293%. The $0.32 is about a fifth of the quarter's $1.54. The check is covered, and it is the small piece. What would put Schwab on the Income Len5: a dividend well above 1.31% of $97.74 that the quarter's profit still covers.

The company has set Thursday, October 15, for the quarter's financial report. The investor update that day runs 8:30am to 9:30am ET, with chief executive Rick Wurster and chief financial officer Mike Verdeschi. It starts an hour before the regular session and ends as that session opens. TipRanks' consensus is $1.67 a share against $1.31 in the year-ago quarter. That is an analyst figure, not a number the company has guided. The line that separates a higher yield helping from clients moving cash out is net interest revenue against the June quarter's $3.357B.

Public posts over the last day were heavy and leaned slightly up. The closes went the other way. Loud attention is not a figure from the business.

Charley is an assistant Schwab owns. It does not set the rate on idle cash. That rate sits inside the October 15 net interest figure, and the shares are $2.61 under the close from the morning the Fed's 10-year was still 4.96%.

Not investment advice.

quoted_tweet.text:
WHAT BROKE AT 9:30? SCHWAB $SCHW IS DOWN 6% AND THE BOND MARKET NEVER MOVED:

Charles Schwab (SCHW) at $100.36, -$6.52 / -6.10% today. The Westlake, Texas company is the largest US retail brokerage: it holds the accounts, the cash and the record-keeping for ordinary investors and for more than 16,000 independent financial advice firms.

The read an hour in: this open sold the companies paid to hold other people's money, sorted by how much of their income comes from that job. What makes it worth stopping on is what did not happen. Bank shares normally fall because interest rates moved. Rates did not move.

Before the bell this looked like a Dow morning. The Dow-tracking fund was bid to $523.52 at 9:10am ET, about 0.7% above Monday, while the technology fund sat slightly red. At the bell all of it turned over. Against Monday's closes:

- SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA): $517.27, -$2.51 / -0.48%. It opened at $522.47, the highest it has traded all day, and has handed back a full 1.0% from that print.
- Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), the hundred largest Nasdaq names: $744.43, +$2.96 / +0.40%. It opened under Monday at $740.98 and is the only one of the four up from its open.
- iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM), the smallest US companies: $286.29, +$0.71 / +0.25%, after opening at $287.67. Half the premarket small-company bid is gone.
- SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY): $773.14, -$0.36 / -0.05%. Flat, because one sector is cancelling the rest out.

That sector is finance. Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF) at $54.79, -$1.11 / -1.99%. Its high for the day, $56.04, was set in the opening minutes and has not been touched since.

Rank the damage, because the order is the argument:

- LPL Financial Holdings (LPLA) at $311.39, -$20.87 / -6.28%, and Schwab at -6.10%. Both are paid to hold client cash and serve advisors.
- Raymond James Financial (RJF) at $156.53, -$8.66 / -5.24%. Same shape, advisor-led.
- JPMorgan Chase (JPM) at $339.12, -$12.92 / -3.67%, and Goldman Sachs (GS) at $937.57, -$21.83 / -2.27%. These two are most of the Dow's problem, because the Dow weights members by share price rather than company size, and between them they gave up $34.75 of it this morning.
- Robinhood Markets (HOOD) at $123.36, +$0.06 / +0.05%. Unchanged.

Of those five, only Raymond James is a current Len5 pick, 12th of the 91 names on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5, which hunts a sound business knocked down by a fixable problem: it holds a sticky base of advisors, and this morning is the knock-down. The other four are on none of the six.

Rates are not the excuse. iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) at $81.71, -$0.09 / -0.11%. That fund rises when long-term interest rates fall and drops when they rise, and today it has done neither. The only scheduled number landed at 10:00am ET, half an hour after the selling started: the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond's September factory survey for its five-state district came in at -2, against a consensus of 5 and August's 4. Above zero means more factories reported growing than shrinking, so -2 is a mild contraction - and a soft regional factory reading does not take 6% off a brokerage.

The business being sold is not a struggling one. Schwab's July 21 report, for the three months to June 30: revenue $7.07B, +20.9% from $5.85B; net income $2.80B, +31.7%, about 40 cents kept from every revenue dollar; adjusted profit $1.62 a share against $1.51 expected, a seventh straight quarter above estimates. On September 15 it said client assets hit $13.41T at the end of August, +19% in a year.

What is being repriced is not the assets. It is what Schwab earns on the cash inside them. A brokerage sweeps idle customer cash into its own bank, pays the customer very little, and keeps the difference. On September 8, BofA Securities analyst Craig Siegenthaler put numbers to it: Schwab paid 0.01% on swept cash in August against 3.35% at Robinhood Gold, and roughly 57% of its forecast 2027 revenue comes from that spread. He rates it underperform at a $91 target and models 2027 revenue down about 5% as customers connect outside software to their accounts and pull cash out - while saying he does not see this as a near-term earnings event. This trade has run before: on February 10, after a private firm launched an AI tax-planning tool, Raymond James fell 8.8% and Schwab 7.4%.

Schwab is a pick on none of the six Len5es. The nearest is Quality-Value, which hunts a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought for less than it is worth. The rebuild half is plainly there - $13.41T of custody and 33,000 employees is not assembled from scratch. The price half fails, at about 19 times the past year's profit and 4.2 times its net worth on its own books, even after this fall. What would put Schwab on the Quality-Value Len5: profit still compounding at this pace several quarters out with the share price no higher than today, which is exactly what the cash-spread argument disputes.

Robinhood is the comparison that makes the sorting look like a judgment rather than noise. The Menlo Park broker built its accounts so an outside AI model can research and place trades, opened that to paying subscribers on May 27, and pays 3.35% on swept cash instead of earning the spread. It is flat this morning while the two firms that earn the spread are down more than 6%. It is a pick on none of the six Len5es either: at roughly 62 times the $1.99 a share analysts model for this year, no value-minded Len5 has a discount to weigh.

Hold the hour loosely. Three Federal Reserve officials speak today, Thomas Barkin last at 1:00pm ET, alongside a Treasury sale of 2-year notes at the same hour.

Eight days ago Schwab told its advisors it was handing them an AI assistant. This morning the market decided the assistant is the competition. Both cannot be right, and the figure that separates them - what Schwab earns on $13.41T of other people's money - is published October 15 before the open, a date the company has confirmed, with $1.67 a share expected against $1.31 a year ago.

Not investment advice.

🚀 Something I’ve been building is almost ready.

On October 8, 2026, I’m officially launching ModuAI.

A new way for businesses to work with AI — not just another chatbot.

ModuAI is built around AI employees that can help businesses manage tasks, workflows, knowledge, reports, and everyday operations.

🌎 Built for businesses worldwide.

📅 October 8 — Launch Day

This is only the beginning.

Follow along. The launch is coming. 🚀

#ModuAI #AI #SaaS #Startup #FutureOfWork

Talked to a YC founder who built an AI product analytics tool and signed 40 customers in his first quarter.

Without ads, content and warm intros. 

Just one simple insight about tech stacks.

Step 1: 

Everyone looks at what tools a company uses. 
He looks at what's missing.

His ideal customer wasn't a company using Mixpanel.

It was a company that should be using something like Mixpanel, but isn't yet.

Step 2: 

He built lists of companies running:

Google Analytics + Hotjar + Google Tag Manager

But no Segment. No Mixpanel.

He is looking for team that cares about data, are watching heat maps and pageviews, but have zero visibility into what users actually do inside the product.

They've outgrown their stack but they just haven't admitted it yet.

Step 3: 

He splits by maturity.

WordPress + GA + Hotjar = a marketing-led company. 

Pitch: "Understand which visitors become real users."

Shopify + GA + Hotjar = an e-commerce brand. 

Pitch: "See exactly where buyers drop off between product page and checkout."

Same gap but way different messaging. 

Step 4: 

Reach out to the Head of Growth with a mini-audit.

Opening line:

"Noticed you're using Hotjar and GA but nothing for product events. Curious how you're tracking activation today?"

Most of them answered with some version of: "Honestly? Spreadsheets."

Step 5: 

31% reply rate. 1 in 5 replies turned into a demo.

Your best prospects might be defined by the tool they're missing, not the one they have.

You can run this exact playbook with @GojiberryAI.

Filter companies by the tech they use, spot the gaps, find the right decision-makers, and launch outreach in a few clicks.

If this helps another founder, feel free to share it 🙏

items.text:
En marge du #FIFAfrica26, le consortium #DigitaliseYouth a mis sur la table ce que 14 pays ont appris sur le terrain : les obstacles, les avancées, et des recommandations politiques concrètes pour une participation des jeunes vraiment effective. 🗣️

#AfricTivistes, représentée par Aisha Dabo (@mashanubian ), y a porté le thème de la participation citoyenne en ligne, aux côtés de ses partenaires : @Code4Africa a ouvert le débat sur l'IA et la souveraineté des données, tandis que des bénéficiaires du projet venus du Cameroun 🇨🇲 et du Niger 🇳🇪 ont partagé leur vécu sur l'accès aux outils numériques et la construction de coalitions pour le changement.

Des recommandations portées par celles et ceux qui les vivent. Prochaine étape : les faire adopter par les gouvernements, les plateformes et la société civile. 👊🏾

Une même conviction : l'espace civique numérique se défend, et il se construit.

📖 Relire notre article de lancement du projet : https://t.co/oCJrwcZgVB

⚡ Propulsé par Digital Democracy Initiative  

-----------------------------------

On the sidelines of #FIFAfrica26, the #DigitaliseYouth consortium put on the table what 14 countries have learnt on the ground: the obstacles, the progress and concrete policy recommendations for youth participation that truly counts. 🗣️

#AfricTivistes, represented by Aisha Dabo, led the theme of online citizen participation alongside its partners: Code for Africa opened the debate on AI and data sovereignty, whilst project beneficiaries from Cameroon 🇨🇲 and Niger 🇳🇪 shared their experience of accessing digital tools and building coalitions for change.

Recommendations shaped by those who live them. Next step: getting them adopted by governments, platforms and civil society. 👊🏾

One shared conviction: digital civic space must be defended, and built.

📖 Revisit our project launch article: https://t.co/oCJrwcZgVB

⚡ Powered by the Digital Democracy Initiative
